title: Maximum Score Of Spliced Array
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2, both of the same length, you can choose two integers left and right such that 0 <= left <= right < n and swap the subarray nums1[left...right] with the subarray nums2[left...right].
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2, both of the same length, you can choose two integers left and right such that 0 <= left <= right < n and swap the subarray nums1[left...right] with the subarray nums2[left...right]. For example, if nums1 = [1,2,3,4,5] and nums2 = [11,12,13,14,15] and you choose left = 1 and right = 2, nums1 becomes [1,12,13,4,5] and nums2 becomes [11,2,3,14,15]. The score of the arrays is the maximum of the sums of nums1 and nums2. Return the highest possible score by performing at most one such swap.
constraints: Choose one contiguous interval and swap that interval between the arrays; choosing no beneficial swap is allowed.
Return the largest possible sum of either array after the swap.
hints: View swapping an interval into nums1 as adding the interval sum of nums2[i]-nums1[i].
Use Kadane’s algorithm to find the maximum nonnegative interval gain.
Compute the gain in both directions and add it to the corresponding original sum.
Every legal swap corresponds to one difference-array interval, so the best of both directional maximum subarrays is exact.
editorial: Every legal swap corresponds to one difference-array interval, so the best of both directional maximum subarrays is exact.

tests.explanation: Swapping the middle element into the first array produces a sum of two hundred ten.
The best exchanged interval raises one array sum to two hundred twenty.
